spec.title: Graph notes, deferred instructions and recoverable Trash

status.comment: Owner additions during productization: capture ideas against future graph work without interrupting the current agent, and preserve removed objects and notes in Trash.

p.anchored-notes: A human can attach a passive note or deferred instruction to a project, semantic object, relationship or work/agent reference. Its stable target contains project/context, reference domain and exact source reference; its recorded basis and object snapshot explain what the author saw. Note identity, author, versions, timestamps and history are durable shared-server data. Layout coordinates, labels and similarity are never routing identity. Passive notes do not dispatch agent input. Editing an instruction creates a new version rather than rewriting previously delivered content.

p.deferred-delivery: The default deferred trigger is before work begins on the exact bound task or milestone. Creating a note does not interrupt the active task, start a model, or silently change the plan. Managed launch and an explicit host-neutral begin-work protocol resolve known work targets and retrieve eligible instructions before work. Native work that has not declared a target remains visibly waiting for a matching work boundary; Zap does not guess the target from natural-language output. Queued, offered, read/acknowledged and explicitly resolved states remain distinct. Delivery is versioned and idempotent for the addressed work attempt, respecting pause, stop, authority and source changes.

p.human-control: The human can view, edit, archive or explicitly send a deferred instruction now. A note, ordinary reply or acknowledgement is not execution permission, Owner approval or proof of implementation. Agent feedback may explain that an instruction was considered, superseded or needs clarification, without erasing the original. Automatic suggestions of obsolescence remain distinguishable from a human archive action.

p.trash: Trash is a recoverable shared collection scoped by project/context, with an authorized cross-project overview. It retains removed graph objects together with their notes and relevant source snapshot, relationships, former identity, plan/source basis, removal reason, actor and time. Individually archived or obsolete notes are retained too. Moving an item to Trash stops its deferred delivery. The current product has no irreversible deletion action for these records. Filters, collapsed regions, paginated/partial snapshots and temporarily unavailable data do not prove source deletion and cannot archive items.

p.replanning: An authoritative source removal or replacement preserves the old object and its attachments in Trash or an explicit unresolved-target state. Missing or changed targets are not silently relinked by matching names. The human can inspect the former context, restore an eligible note, or explicitly relink it to a current exact object. An unchanged stable identity can retain notes across new plan revisions while showing their recorded source basis. Delivery checks whether the current target and instruction version remain eligible.

p.restoration: Restoring a note is a versioned annotation operation with history and current-target validation. It does not replay an acknowledged instruction or restart completed work. Restoring an old semantic plan object is a proposal through the ordinary ZAP planning/admission path, not a write to a graph cache or resurrection of an old active plan. Restoring a visual board arrangement changes presentation only. These operations have different labels and outcomes in the UI.

p.shared-implementation: The shared application service owns annotation versions, target resolution, delivery eligibility and Trash. Lens clients render the same scoped records and named commands. Coordinator/managed backend work transitions consume a shared future-work attachment port rather than a Quick Lens-only queue. Source observers archive only on sufficient authoritative evidence. Notes and Trash survive client disconnects, provider changes and ordinary account/session continuity.
